output.brief: Store 14's rise from 1.5% to 2.3% may not be a real change in losses. The figures are estimates taken from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across the chain, about half of two-quarter rises of this size were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full counts have been steady at 1.5–1.8%. The rise is spread across all departments and sales mix hasn't changed, so a mix shift doesn't explain it. The shoplifting log counts rose chain-wide after the incident app launched on 1 April, so that rise is not good evidence of more theft. The night-stocker tip was checked on CCTV and not supported. Self-checkout, shoplifting and staff theft remain unproven. Two neighbouring stores without self-checkout show no similar rise. That is weak support for a store-specific change, but it doesn't settle the cause. Recommended next step: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and decline Regional Operations' proposal to drop it. Hold off on guards, pulling the lanes, or action against the night stocker until the count result is compared with the estimates. If the count confirms a real rise, then test self-checkout, customer theft and staff theft directly. Confidence is moderate to high on the count decision and low on the cause.
